question: Should a recording's own sound bar take its picture's colours, so the two read as one clip?
context: The sound a recording came with now sits on a row right under its picture (asked for on 2026-10-13). Its bar is joined to the picture by a staple and a link mark, but keeps the green all sound wears.

options.label: Keep sound green, joined by a staple
options.summary: The sound under a recording stays the dark green every sound wears, joined to its picture bar by a short cyan staple and a link mark. This is what ships today.
pros: Sound always looks like sound, wherever it is
cons: The picture bar is blue and its sound green, so they look like two things side by side
options.mitigation: The staple and link mark sit right where the two bars start.

options.label: Tint the attached sound like its picture
options.summary: A recording's own sound bar under its picture takes a darker shade of the picture's blue to violet, so picture and sound read as one clip in two parts. A detached sound goes back to green.
pros: One clip reads as one thing at a glance
Detaching visibly changes the colour, which says the link broke
cons: Departs from the sound mock's colours
The waveform and volume line must stay readable on the new shade
options.mitigation: Only attached sound changes; music and detached sound keep the mock's colours.

options.label: Leave it as it is, no more work
options.summary: Nothing changes and this question is closed.
options.mitigation: You can ask again any time.

answer.note: Taken as recommended: the user, 2026-10-19, said there were too many cards, most did not matter and they could not follow them. Change it later only if they complain about the result
